# S596 — when two changed files depend on each other's new fields, write a base overlay that reverts both together

**Findings:**  · **Size:**  · **Tree:**

**2026-11-25** — Also covers adj 588: when every single-file base overlay fails to build (a shared signature change), offer one overlay that reverts all changed product files together, alongside the per-file ones. Jon chose 'Two slices', session 8d711f67, 2026-11-25.

trust: unverified; by: Jon Robbins

**Not in this slice:**

## Why

The reviewer reported this as tool feedback (friction) on ork in run ork-20261125-204703-eec0, item S580. Two changed files each depend on a field the other adds. Reverting one file alone leaves the package uncompilable, so every single-file overlay fails. The evidence: `overlay-1.json` failed with `view.go:341 m.roadmapLift undefined`, and `overlay-2.json` failed with `model.go:1208 d.total undefined`. The same thing happened in S587 (adj 588): all four Base overlays entries said "does not build" because `baseOverlaySection`, `untestedCallSitesSection` and `branchChangeResult` change together. S593 made ork say "does not build" for such an entry. The reviewer still has no revert command in that case and must trace every base version by hand.

Owner decision, 2026-11-25 (adj 588, folded into this slice; Jon chose "Two slices", session 8d711f67): when every single-file base overlay fails to build, ork also offers one overlay that reverts all the changed product Go files together. It sits alongside the per-file entries, which stay as they are. Like the rest of the section, it is advisory and never blocks the run.

Owner decision, 2026-11-25 (adj 588 folded here): offer the combined overlay only when at least two overlays were written and every one fails the build check.

## Failing tests

All new tests are in `internal/engine/baseoverlay_test.go`. They use `overlayVetHarness` or `newHarness`, and `overlayVetResult`, to route fake `go vet` replies. The harness answers the n-th vet call with `Seq[n]`, so the per-file vets come first in sorted order and the combined vet is the last call. A new helper finds the combined entry: the line that starts `- All changed Go files at once`. `baseOverlayEntries` only counts lines that start with `- ` and a backtick, so it does not count this line.
- TestBaseOverlayAllTogetherWhenEverySingleFileFails: changed `internal/y/b.go` and `internal/x/a.go`, both present in the base. The vet replies are fail, fail, then success. There are exactly three vet calls. The third is `-C WORKTREE vet -overlay TMPDIR/overlay-all.json ./internal/x ./internal/y`. `TMPDIR/overlay-all.json` parses to a `Replace` map holding both `WORKTREE/internal/x/a.go` and `WORKTREE/internal/y/b.go`, each mapped to its `TMPDIR/base/...` copy. The two per-file entries still read `does not build: ...` with no command. The combined entry names `go -C WORKTREE test -overlay TMPDIR/overlay-all.json ./internal/x ./internal/y`. No line holds a pipe. The intro text "only that file reverted" is absent, because no single-file command remains.
- TestBaseOverlayAllTogetherNotOfferedWhenOneFileBuilds: two files; the vet replies are fail, then success. There are two vet calls, no `overlay-all.json`, and no `All changed Go files` entry.
- TestBaseOverlayAllTogetherNeedsTwoFiles: one changed file whose vet fails. There is one vet call, no `overlay-all.json`, and no combined entry.
- TestBaseOverlayAllTogetherThatDoesNotBuildIsReported: two files; every vet reply fails (the last reply repeats). The combined entry reads `does not build: ` followed by the bounded diagnostic and a `git show` pointer, and it has no test command. `overlay-all.json` still exists for inspection.
- TestBaseOverlayAllTogetherMapsNewFileToEmpty: one file new in the slice (`git show` says not in base) and one existing file; every per-file vet fails and the combined vet succeeds. In `overlay-all.json` the new file maps to `""` and the existing file maps to its base copy. No base copy is written for the new file.
- TestBaseOverlayNoIntroWhenNothingBuilds (edited): both per-file vets and the combined vet fail. The section now has `does not build: undefined helper` three times, two per-file lines and one combined line. It still holds none of `go -C`, `-run NAME` and `Each command runs`.

## Implement

1. In `internal/engine/baseoverlay.go`, change `overlayBuildError` to take the packages as a variadic `pkgs ...string` and pass them all after the overlay file in the `go vet` arguments. The single-package call is unchanged.
2. Change `writeBaseOverlay` to also return the `Replace` key (`WORKTREE/path`) and the replacement value (the `TMPDIR/base/path` copy, or `""` for a new file). It still writes `overlay-N.json` as before.
3. In `baseOverlaySection`, collect each written overlay's key and value, and its `packageArg`, as the loop runs.
4. After the loop, when at least two overlays were written and every one of them failed the vet (the per-file `commands` count is zero), write `TMPDIR/overlay-all.json`. Its content is `{"Replace": {...}}` with every collected key and value. Use `json.Marshal`, mode 0o600, and a trailing newline.
5. Run `overlayBuildError` on `overlay-all.json` with the sorted, de-duplicated list of the packages of all those files, using the same `baseOverlayVetTimeout`.
6. Append one entry after the per-file entries, starting `- All changed Go files at once (N files)`.
   - On success the entry names `go -C WORKTREE test -overlay TMPDIR/overlay-all.json PKG1 PKG2 ...`, built with `ShellWord`. It says that no single-file overlay builds, so this one reverts every file listed above together. It also says to add `-run NAME` before the package list, one test per command, and never a `-run` pattern that joins names.
   - On a vet failure the entry reads `does not build: MESSAGE. Trace the base versions with `git show` instead.`
   - A vet that cannot run or times out leaves the command in place, as for the per-file entries.
7. Leave the intro paragraph tied to the per-file command count. The combined entry carries its own guidance, so it is self-contained when no per-file command exists. Files left out past the 20-file cap and files whose base could not be read are not in the combined overlay; the existing left-out and incomplete notices stay.
8. In `internal/engine/baseoverlay_test.go`, write the five new tests first and watch them fail. Then edit `TestBaseOverlayNoIntroWhenNothingBuilds` for the third `does not build` line. The other existing tests pass as they are, because the harness default vet route exits 0.
9. In `docs/design.md`, in the `## Base overlays` bullet (lines 2041-2066), add one sentence marked S596 and adj 588. It says: when at least two overlays were written and every one fails the vet, ork writes `TMPDIR/overlay-all.json` reverting all those files, vets it over their packages, and lists it as a final entry with a test command (or `does not build: ERROR`).
10. Add the changelog entry with `slicer changelog add S596 --text "..."`. Do not edit `CHANGELOG.md`.
